rm_teen_first_kiss.text: You and {{name}} are alone on the porch steps. The silence is loud, and so is your pulse.

outcomes.sweet: It is brief, clumsy and perfect. You float home.
outcomes.clash: You misjudge the angle and bump noses. {{name}} laughs, then you both laugh, then it gets awkward.

rm_teen_sneak_out.text: {{name}} texts at midnight: come outside, the stars are out. Your parents' bedroom door is thirty feet from the front door.

outcomes.magic: You sit on a curb and talk until the sky goes grey. Best night of your year.
outcomes.caught: The porch light snaps on. You are grounded until further notice.

rm_teen_dance_ask.text: The school dance is in two weeks. {{name}} keeps mentioning it in a way that is not subtle at all.

outcomes.yes: {{name}} says yes before you finish the sentence. You rent a suit that almost fits.
outcomes.stage: You pick a public spot, which turns out to be a mistake. {{name}} says yes, but the audience will remember.

rm_date_jealous.text: {{name}} has noticed that you laugh differently around a coworker. You haven't. Probably.

outcomes.fine: {{name}} and the coworker bond over hating the same sports team. Crisis dissolved.
outcomes.worse: It goes badly. {{name}} watches you the whole evening like a hawk with a clipboard.

rm_date_meet_parents.text: {{name}} wants you to meet the parents. There will be a roast. You will be the roast.

outcomes.loved: {{name}}'s mother asks if you are staying for dessert. That is the highest honour.
outcomes.flop: You call their father by the wrong name twice. Nobody mentions it, which is worse.

rm_date_move_in.text: {{name}} brings up moving in together. Two toothbrushes, one lease, and one very large decision.

outcomes.bliss: Boxes, takeout and a couch that does not fit through the door. You are happy.
outcomes.friction: Within a week you've fought about dishes, towels and the thermostat. Love continues, loudly.

rm_date_proposal.text: {{name}} cooks your favourite meal and is oddly sweaty. Halfway through dessert, {{name}} drops to one knee and holds out a ring.

rm_date_anniversary.text: Your anniversary with {{name}} is tomorrow. You know this because a calendar alert told you, and you love that alert.

outcomes.both: {{name}} forgot as well. You split a pizza and a guilty look.
outcomes.oops: {{name}} did not forget. The silence at dinner is a three-course meal.

rm_date_ex_text.text: Your phone buzzes with a message from an old flame. {{name}} is sitting right beside you and has very good eyesight.

outcomes.harmless: It's a polite exchange about a mutual friend's baby. Nothing happens, mostly.
outcomes.caught: {{name}} reads it over your shoulder. The temperature in the room drops ten degrees.

rm_date_getaway.text: You and {{name}} get a long weekend. Somewhere with a beach and no deadlines is calling.

outcomes.dream: Sun, sand, bad umbrella drinks. You come back relaxed and slightly sunburnt.
outcomes.rain: It rains four days straight. You play board games in the hotel and somehow grow closer.

rm_date_money_talk.text: {{name}} asks about your finances over breakfast. Spreadsheets have entered the relationship.

outcomes.solid: You get one tidy account and a shared budget. It's mildly romantic.
outcomes.bills: You find out about {{name}}'s subscriptions. All of them. {{name}} finds out about yours too.

rm_date_cheat_scare.text: A friend says they saw {{name}} at a restaurant with a stranger. It could be nothing. It could also be everything.

outcomes.innocent: It was a cousin. You were wrong. {{name}} knows you looked.
outcomes.guilty: The messages are real. You pack a bag with shaking hands.

rm_mar_dishes_fight.text: {{name}} left the dishes in the sink for the third day. You are not speaking, but your silence is incredibly loud.

outcomes.agree: You make a chore chart. It is the most romantic piece of paper you have ever made.
outcomes.fight: It turns into a fight about every dish since your wedding.

rm_mar_anniversary.text: It's your wedding anniversary. {{name}} remembers the date, the restaurant and the exact dessert you shared that night.

outcomes.grace: {{name}} laughs. You are forgiven in exchange for a very long massage.
outcomes.hurt: {{name}} nods slowly. 'All these years,' they say, and leave it there.

rm_mar_inlaws.text: The in-laws are coming for two weeks. {{name}} has already warned them about your cooking. Nobody asked them to comment on it.

outcomes.respect: The in-laws grudgingly back down. {{name}} looks at you like you slayed a dragon.
outcomes.feud: A feud begins that will outlive the pickles in the fridge.

rm_mar_temptation.text: A charming colleague keeps finding reasons to stand close at the coffee machine. {{name}} is at home, folding laundry, trusting you.

outcomes.nothing: Nothing comes of it, except a guilty conscience that goes everywhere with you.
outcomes.affair: It turns into something. Secrets are heavy and cost a lot to carry.

rm_mar_ultimatum.text: {{name}} sits you down at the kitchen table. 'We fix this,' they say, 'or I'm done.' They are not smiling.

outcomes.saved: You go to counselling and actually listen. The marriage steadies, slowly.
outcomes.hollow: You promise a lot. Three weeks later, it's clear it's too late. The paperwork arrives.

rm_mar_money_fight.text: A credit card statement lands on the table. {{name}} circles one line item with a pen and raises an eyebrow.

outcomes.works: For a while, it's all coupons and togetherness. It actually saves money.
outcomes.rebel: By week two, you've both hidden snacks from each other.

rm_mar_date_night.text: It's been months since you and {{name}} did anything that wasn't chores or logistics. A date night is overdue.

rm_mar_illness.text: {{name}} catches something nasty and looks pitiful under three blankets. You are suddenly nurse, cook and chauffeur.

rm_mar_surprise_trip.text: {{name}} hands you a passport and a suitcase. 'Don't ask,' they say. You ask anyway.

outcomes.lovely: A mountain cabin and a week of nothing. You didn't know how badly you needed it.
outcomes.disaster: The cabin has no heat and one spider. You tell the story for years.

rm_mar_midlife.text: You wake at 3 a.m. wondering if this is the life you wanted. {{name}} snores gently beside you, unaware of your existential crisis.

rm_mar_vow_renewal.text: {{name}} suggests renewing your vows. The thought of a second ceremony makes you tear up before the first hymn.

rm_mar_job_offer.text: {{name}} gets a dream job offer in a city across the country. Your life is here, but your spouse's dream is there.

outcomes.thrive: New city, new start. You find a decent bakery and a better life.
outcomes.lonely: The city is expensive and cold. You miss home, but {{name}} is thrilled.

fa_kid_first_steps.text: {{name}} lets go of the couch and wobbles toward you. Your phone is in the other room, which is a tragedy.

fa_kid_school_trouble.text: The school calls. {{name}} was caught passing notes that were, frankly, quite creative, and set off a small fire in the art room.

outcomes.fair: The teacher admits the supplies were poorly labelled. The fire gets a footnote.
outcomes.unfair: Turns out the evidence is airtight. You look silly.

fa_kid_science_fair.text: {{name}} has a science fair project due tomorrow and a volcano that won't erupt. It's 9 p.m.

outcomes.learns: {{name}} improvises with a different chemical. The volcano goes off. They get a ribbon.
outcomes.fails: The volcano doesn't erupt. {{name}} cries a little and you feel awful.

fa_kid_teen_rebel.text: {{name}} dyes their hair green, comes home late, and tells you that you don't understand. You do. That's the scariest part.

outcomes.deal: A midnight curfew, in exchange for the hair. You both call it a win.
outcomes.rejected: {{name}} rolls their eyes so hard it echoes. The deal is off.

fa_kid_driving.text: {{name}} just got a learner's permit. You are sitting in the passenger seat with your hands pressed on the dashboard.

outcomes.pass: After eight parking lots and one traffic cone, {{name}} drives like a pro.
outcomes.crash: There is a small crunch. The mailbox will never be the same.

fa_kid_college_money.text: {{name}} got into a good college. The tuition letter arrives the same day and it has more zeros than hope.

fa_kid_graduation.text: {{name}} walks across the stage in a gown two sizes too big. You clap far too hard and nobody can stop you.

fa_kid_moves_out.text: {{name}} packs the last box into a car that sounds unwell. Their room is suddenly very quiet, and so are you.

fa_kid_money_ask.text: {{name}} calls with a request. They need a loan, 'just until payday'. You have been through this before, with different lunches.

outcomes.paid: They pay you back in full, with a thank-you card. You frame it.
outcomes.gone: The money disappears into a vague plan. You let it go, like most parents.

fa_kid_grandchild_hint.text: {{name}} turns up with a nervous grin and an announcement. You'd guess the news before they reach the second sentence.

fa_parent_aging.text: {{name}} forgets a few words and loses the car keys twice in a week. She laughs it off, but the laugh is thin.

fa_parent_hospital.text: The hospital calls: {{name}} had a fall and needs rest. You're listed as the emergency contact, a role you didn't know you'd taken.

outcomes.comfort: {{name}} gets a better recovery and a view of the car park. They are grateful.
outcomes.bills: The invoice is longer than the stay. You frame the final line, then cry.

fa_parent_move_in.text: {{name}} can't manage the house alone anymore. There's a spare room, a lot of stairs and no easy answer.

outcomes.warm: The house fills with her stories and her unrequested organising. You get used to it.
outcomes.friction: Love, yes. Also, a rearranged kitchen and a daily opinion on your laundry.

fa_parent_inheritance.text: {{name}}'s will is read. Nobody expected the surprise lines about the fishing cabin or the antique clock.

outcomes.win: You win the cabin, and lose a few cousins in the process. The lake is lovely.
outcomes.lose: Legal fees swallow the cabin. Everyone is furious, including the lawyer.

fa_sib_estranged.text: {{name}} hasn't spoken to you in four years, thanks to one argument about a wedding toast. A message pops up out of nowhere: 'Hi.'

outcomes.mend: You talk for two hours. Both of you apologise. Neither of you remembers why it started.
outcomes.cold: The call is stiff and polite. It could go either way from here.

fa_sib_loan.text: {{name}} needs money to cover rent. They swear it's temporary. They swore that last time too.

outcomes.repaid: {{name}} repays you early and buys you dinner. You almost fall off your chair.
outcomes.never: The money vanishes. So does the topic at every family dinner.

fa_sib_wedding.text: {{name}} asks you to be best man or maid of honour. There is a speech involved, and a lot of expectations.

outcomes.tears: The room cries. {{name}} hugs you so hard your glasses fog.
outcomes.bomb: Your joke about their ex lands badly. The silence is loud and long.

fa_sib_reunion.text: You and {{name}} end up in your childhood home, sorting old boxes. A photo falls out of a drawer, and both of you go quiet.

fa_friend_loan.text: {{name}} asks to borrow $800 for 'a thing'. You know their thing and its history.

outcomes.repaid: They repay you in full, plus a bottle of wine. Maybe the thing was real.
outcomes.burned: The money never returns. Neither does the wine, because there was none.

fa_friend_wedding.text: {{name}} is getting married and wants you in the front row. The invite says 'black tie.' You own a tie, sort of.

fa_friend_loyalty.text: Someone at a party says awful things about {{name}} behind their back, and everyone's looking at you to join in.

outcomes.unseen: Nobody tells {{name}}. You feel awful anyway.
outcomes.found_out: Someone tells {{name}}. Your friendship takes a very long, slow breath.

fa_friend_betrayal.text: You find out {{name}} took credit for your idea at work. The pitch was yours. Their smile at the meeting was theirs.

outcomes.justice: The boss believes you. {{name}} is quietly sidelined and your friendship is over.
outcomes.backfire: It turns into a messy he-said she-said. You both lose, and the friendship with it.

fa_friend_secret.text: {{name}} tells you a secret in a whisper, then looks at you with huge eyes. 'Don't tell anyone.' Someone else will ask by Friday.

outcomes.small: You tell one person. They tell no one. Probably.
outcomes.spread: It spreads like a rumour in a small town. {{name}} knows exactly where it started.

fa_friend_moves_away.text: {{name}} announces they're moving across the country for a job. Your standing weekly coffee is about to become a weekly video call.

fa_friend_road_trip.text: {{name}} swings by with a beat-up car and a plan: a weekend road trip, no destination. The snacks are already packed.

outcomes.epic: You sing badly, laugh loudly and get lost twice. The photos are terrible and priceless.
outcomes.breakdown: The car dies in a remote village. You spend the night in a diner learning someone's life story.

fa_friend_business.text: {{name}} pitches a business idea: a subscription box for socks. You think it might be good. You're also not sure about the socks.

outcomes.profit: The socks sell like hotcakes. Weird, but your bank account loves it.
outcomes.loss: Nobody wants subscription socks. The garage is full of them now.

rm_single_meet_cute.text: You and a stranger reach for the same last avocado at the market. Eye contact lasts a beat too long.

outcomes.spark: They laugh at your joke about guacamole. By the time you leave, you have a number and a plan.
outcomes.nope: They're polite, married, and in a hurry. You go home with one avocado and a lesson.

rm_single_app_disaster.text: A dating app sets you up with someone whose photos are twelve years old and whose conversation is entirely about their ex.

outcomes.kind: They shrug, thank you and order dessert for the road.
outcomes.scene: They make a loud scene about 'wasted time.' You leave a tip for the staff.

rm_single_blind_date.text: A friend insists you'd adore their cousin. 'Trust me,' they say. This is the sentence that precedes most disasters.

outcomes.match: It's easy and funny and the cousin is wonderful. Your friend gloats for a week.
outcomes.bust: There's no chemistry, just a long talk about tax forms. The cousin leaves with a handshake.

rm_single_wedding_plus_one.text: Another wedding invitation arrives. The card has a space for 'plus one', and it's staring at you like an unpaid bill.

outcomes.spark: The two of you dance badly and notice each other differently. Something starts.
outcomes.fun: You have a great time. No sparks, but the buffet was lovely.

rm_single_cafe_regular.text: There's someone at your regular cafe who orders the same drink and sits in the same corner. You've accidentally memorised their schedule.

outcomes.coffee: You swap names and numbers. A real date follows. The barista tips off the whole staff.
outcomes.awkward: They are wearing headphones and don't hear you. You wave at the wall instead.

rm_single_ghosted.text: A promising date turns into three days of silence. Your phone sits face up on the table like a pet awaiting news.

outcomes.reply: They reply, apologise, and actually explain. You decide to forgive them.
outcomes.void: The message goes unanswered. You realise it was for you, not them.

rm_ex_text.text: Your phone lights up: {{name}}, your ex, saying 'Thinking of you'. It's 1 a.m. and you are weak.

outcomes.closure: You talk for an hour and both feel lighter. Then goodbye, politely.
outcomes.messy: Old wounds pop open like a bad zip. You regret it by morning.

rm_ex_wedding_invite.text: An invitation arrives in the mail. {{name}} is getting married and wants you there. It reads like a polite dare.

rm_ex_bump_into.text: You turn a corner at the grocery store and find {{name}} holding a cart full of cereal. You are holding a cart full of cereal too.

outcomes.nice: The coffee is pleasant. You part as better friends than lovers.
outcomes.awkward: Three sips in, you recall every reason for the breakup. You leave early.

rm_ex_returns.text: {{name}} appears at your door with flowers, an apology and a very rehearsed speech. 'I was wrong,' they say.

outcomes.reunion: The second time goes better. The old fights stay in the past.
outcomes.repeat: Same patterns, new flowers. You learn that people rarely change on a doorstep.
